summary:
Red team of part 1 of the Iwasawa theory and special values area: eight roadmaps and 74 stages (HeegnerPointEulerSystems 12, RankZeroOneBSD 12, AutomorphicCongruences 10, GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights 10, AutomorphicPadicLFunctions 9, EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems 9, ModularIwasawaMainConjectures 7, SelmerIwasawaCohomology 5), with two integrated decompositions, read against parts 2 and 3 and the whole atlas. There are 39 findings: 7 high, 29 medium and 3 low. Most papers routed here were extracted or reviewed by the coordinator, so this red team covers the stage texts and the remaining routes.

The seven high findings:
(1) HE.8's Cornut–Vatsal CM-point distribution rests on S-arithmetic Ratner theory or a proven case of André–Oort, which no stage plans.
(2) The Ribet/Diamond–Taylor level raising behind W. Zhang's theorem (HE.6) has no owner.
(3) GZ.1 re-plans the height machinery and Mordell–Weil for abelian varieties, which the accepted RS-03 keeps in HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0/RP.1.
(4) BSD.6's rank-zero multiplicative case has no supplier for Skinner's p‖N main conjecture, Greenberg–Stevens or the transcendence of q_E.
(5) BSD.7a's Eisenstein branch needs Rubin's main conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields, Hida–Tilouine and Wüthrich's integrality, which nothing plans.
(6) AutomorphicCongruences L1, L2 and L2s use the Galois representations of unitary-group cusp forms (AG2.2, AG2.5, AG2.6) without edges.
(7) No layer plans the mod-p nonvanishing theorems (Hida, Finis, Vatsal, Hsieh) that L3h, Skinner–Urban and Castella–Liu–Wan need.

The medium findings fall into three groups:
- Misplaced or misdescribed routes: FW Theorem 1.6 via FW §4.8 needs L2's constructions but sits in L1; L5a cites the wrong BCS theorem; L5b omits Kato's divisibility; L4e omits Eischen–Wan hypotheses; L2 claims growth not proved over general number fields; ES.8 requires the higher-rank ES.7; SIC L2 has a wrong edge.
- Missing owners: Serre's open-image theorem, Howard's self-dual Kolyvagin systems, the Hida–Tilouine CM main conjecture, nonnegativity of central L-values, p-integrality of the Manin constant, and Greenberg's no-finite-submodule theorem.
- Duplicates: GZ.9 with L3h and GH.1, Yager modules in AC L2 and GH.7, L5a with BSD.6a, SIC L2 with EllipticCurves Layer 7, and SIC L4 with ESCMC L3.

One library claim: GZ.0 misstates Tau Ceti's height normalisation, which is the (O) height and not twice it. The low findings are locator and naming points. The coordinator extracted or reviewed 34 papers mentioning these roadmaps and red-teamed AUDIT-26; neither is re-examined here.

That theorem is Ratner's uniform distribution of unipotent orbits on p-adic Lie groups, the S-arithmetic Ratner theorem. Consumers of the early HE.8 classes inherit the same gap wherever they use that nonvanishing: AutomorphicCongruences:L5a, GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.8, RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6a and BSD.7a.

findings.claim: BSD.6 targets the rank-zero p-part formula at primes of multiplicative reduction, but no layer supplies what that case needs. (1) The cyclotomic main conjecture for p || N. MIMC L1, BSD.6's only main-conjecture supplier, is FW 1.6 with p not dividing N. MIMC L2 (FW 1.7) excludes multiplicative p by its local hypothesis (1), since E[p]|G_Qp has semisimplification chi (+) chi_cyc chi with chi unramified. (2) The Greenberg-Stevens exceptional-zero theorem for the Mazur-Tate-Teitelbaum p-adic L-function at split multiplicative p. (3) Nonvanishing of the L-invariant log_p q_E / ord_p q_E, which rests on the transcendence of the Tate period q_E (Barre-Sirieix-Diaz-Gramain-Philibert). The source that JSW 7.2.1(ii) cites for this branch uses all three. The atlas mentions an exceptional-zero formula only once, as an unowned 'separate construction' in GZ.9, and neither library has an L-invariant or a Tate period.

findings.claim: For non-CM E, HE.7's all-prime finiteness needs Serre's open-image theorem: ρ̄_{E,p} is surjective for all but finitely many p. No layer owns this general theorem. HE.7 names it only as 'required open-image … bounds' inside a Heegner application stage. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.6 explicitly avoids it, and so does EllipticCurveModularity:R29.1 after accepted RS-06. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4 covers only facts about finite subgroups. R29.1's irreducibility for almost all p does not suffice: that an irreducible image in the normalizer of a Cartan cannot occur for large p is exactly Serre's theorem. The clean Heegner theorem assumes surjectivity instead of proving it, and neither library has the theorem. The same gap applies to the Kolyvagin–Logachev RM quotients, which need the GL₂-type analogue.
findings.evidence: HE.7: 'For non-CM curves prove the required open-image/cohomological bounds and their uniformity…' and 'Use the finite index of the non-torsion point in the rank-one Mordell–Weil lattice to prove that Sha[p∞] vanishes for all but finitely many p…'. R28.6: 'R29 uses this to show only finitely many rational prime-degree isogenies without requiring the full Serre open-image theorem or excluding CM curves.' RS-06.result.json, R29.1 keeps: '…do not assume the Serre open-image theorem or exclude CM.' R01.4: 'Prove the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments…'. In data/atlas.json, 'open image'/'open-image' matches only DWP.2, LPV.5, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1, R28.6, HE.7 and tauceti ClassFieldTheory/ProfiniteProPGroups text. None of these plans the elliptic theorem. data/library-coverage.json (AUDIT-25), HE.7 target note: 'Absent: no Galois representations of elliptic curves and no open image theorem'. Howard, arXiv:1202.6340v1, read 2026-09-24, Theorem A, p. 2, takes surjectivity as a hypothesis: 'Assume also that Gal(K̄/K) → Aut_{Z_p}(T) is surjective.'
findings.fix: Plan Serre's open-image theorem for non-CM elliptic curves over number fields once (Serre, Invent. Math. 15 (1972)): ρ̄_{E,p} is surjective for all but finitely many p, and the ℓ-adic images are open. HE's own summary gives 'Kolyvagin-system descent' to ES, and HE.6 says 'Apply the abstract descent engine'. Yet the accepted HE decomposition realises Thm 1.6.1 inside HE.6's node. ES.4's two interfaces are Mazur–Rubin §5.2 and Rubin's error-tolerant version, which Howard says do not contain his §1.4 self-duality results, and ES.5 only remarks on the square-index bound. GH.5 needs the Λ-adic version: Longo–Vigni's Thm 3.5 follows Howard's Thm 2.2.10 under (H.1)–(H.5). GH.5's suppliers are only ES.3, ES.4 and GH.4, so as planned the theory is either built twice (HE and GH) or missing for GH. Separately, the integrated link HE.6-node → HE.8-node (Theorem B 'applying at every prime of Λ the same machinery used to prove Theorem A') has no matching stage edge: HE.8 does not require HE.6.

findings.claim: GZ.0 rests on a false premise about the pinned library. It says the existing elliptic height 'is normalized using the logarithmic x-height, twice one common convention'. At Tau Ceti f790474 the canonical height is half the x-height limit. That is the height attached to the divisor (O), the common convention and not twice it. The pairing is the halved polarisation, so ⟨P,P⟩ = ĥ(P). Compare YZZ's ⟨x,y⟩_L = ĥ_L(x+y)−ĥ_L(x)−ĥ_L(y) with L = O((O)), so ⟨x,x⟩_L = 2ĥ_L(x), as the GZ.1 node records. The library pairing is half of YZZ's. Under GZ.0's premise, the library ĥ would be ĥ_{2(O)} and the two pairings would coincide. So a rank-r Gram determinant differs by 2^r from what the premise predicts. GZ.0 owns the cross-source rescaling conventions (accepted RS-30), so this sign of the power of two reaches the BSD consumers. GZ.0 copies the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves roadmap text, which disagrees with the code. AUDIT-25 records the contradiction at target level, but the stage text is unchanged.
findings.evidence: GZ.0: 'The existing elliptic height is normalized using the logarithmic x-height, twice one common convention. CanonicalHeight.lean:384 neronTatePairing_apply: 'neronTatePairing W P Q = ((P + Q).canonicalHeight - P.canonicalHeight - Q.canonicalHeight) / 2'. CanonicalHeight.lean:390 neronTatePairing_self: '= P.canonicalHeight'. findings.claim: MIMC L1 states the ordinary theorem only in the form of FW Theorem 1.6, and FW 1.6's auxiliary-prime hypothesis is strictly stronger than the Skinner-Urban hypothesis that BSD.6 claims for its rank-zero ordinary branch. FW 1.6 needs ℓ || N with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1 and also dim ρ̄^{G_ℓ} = 0. SU Theorem 1, in the form Skinner restates and BSD.6/JSW 7.2.1(ii) use, needs only a prime q ≠ p, q || N, at which ρ̄ is ramified. The extra condition fails whenever the unramified line of E[p]|G_Qq is Frobenius-fixed, i.e. ψ(q)q ≡ 1 mod p, for example split multiplicative reduction at q with q ≡ 1 mod p. So BSD.6 imports a theorem that does not cover all the curves it claims.

findings.where: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5 and BSD.8 (positivity of the defect)
findings.claim: BSD.5 targets positivity of L*(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_E), and BSD.8 needs a positive defect to conclude defect = 1 from vanishing valuations. No stage supplies the input this needs: nonnegativity of central values L(1/2, π_E ⊗ χ) ≥ 0 for quadratic χ, which follows from Waldspurger, Guo or Lapid-Rallis (n=1). Modular symbols give only rationality, not sign. Gross-Zagier gives only the sign of a product: L'(E/K,1) = L'(E,1)·L(E^K,1) > 0 in rank one and L(E,1)·L'(E^K,1) > 0 in rank zero. GZ.5's toric Waldspurger formula likewise controls only L(E,1)L(E^K,1). So the sign of L*(E,1) is left undetermined in both ranks.
findings.evidence: BSD.5: 'Prove the rationality and positivity of L*(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_E) in analytic ranks 0 and 1: use modular-symbol rationality at rank zero and the Gross–Zagier/period/index comparison at rank one.' BSD.8: 'For the positive nonzero rational BSD defect prove that equality of every prime valuation to zero is equivalent to defect=1.' GZ.5: 'Establish the Waldspurger period formula for the stated GL₂/quaternionic toric data'. A search of data/atlas.json for positivity or nonnegativity of central values, Kohnen-Zagier, or the Shimura/Waldspurger coefficient formula finds nothing. Lapid-Rallis, Ann. of Math. 157 (2003) 891-917, abstract at https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2003/157-3/p05 (read 2026-09-24): 'Let π be a cuspidal generic representation of SO(2n+1, A). We prove that L(1/2, π) ≥ 0.' For n=1, SO(3) ≅ PGL(2), and the standard L-function is that of π_E ⊗ χ_D. See also J. Guo, 'On the positivity of the central critical values of automorphic L-functions for GL(2)', Duke Math. J. 83 (1996), doi:10.1215/S0012-7094-96-08307-6 (Crossref record). Library: Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LSeries (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean:84) is only the Euler product. It has no continuation and no central value.

findings.claim: The p-part formulas compare the Néron period Ω_E with modular-form periods, and that comparison needs p-integrality of the Manin constant. JSW invokes it explicitly, as a result of Mazur: for p ∤ 2ND, p divides neither the Manin constant of E nor that of E^D. No stage plans it. GZ.3 constructs Manin constants only as comparison quantities, and neither library has a Manin constant. Without it, a p-part formula stated with Ω_E follows from the main-conjecture and Gross-Zagier inputs only up to a factor c_E. The same holds for MIMC L3's canonical-period comparison.

findings.claim: L3 owns Iwasawa cohomology and control but does not plan Greenberg's structural theorems for Selmer groups over Q_∞. The first is surjectivity of the global-to-local map defining Sel when X is Λ-torsion and ρ̄ is irreducible. The second is that X, and its Σ-imprimitive versions, has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule, so that its characteristic ideal equals its Fitting ideal. The main-conjecture proofs the area consumes use both. Skinner's p || N deduction depends on them, and Castella's corrected Theorem 1.1 uses their anticyclotomic analogue. No stage plans them.

From this it follows that Ch^Σ_L(f_m) equals the Λ_O-Fitting ideal'. Castella's erratum (URL above), Lemma 2.1 proof: 'This is a special case of Greenberg's general results [Gre16].'
findings.fix: Add to SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 Greenberg's theorems for Greenberg-type Selmer groups over a Z_p-extension. findings.claim: L1 misdescribes the proof route of FW Theorem 1.6. FW does not lift SU's weight restriction itself: it attributes that to Wan's separate Forum Math. FW §4.8 is not a 'period refinement' of the Skinner-Urban U(2,2) argument either. It is a different proof that bypasses the canonical/Gross period comparison. That proof runs through the two-variable Rankin–Selberg Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture over an auxiliary K, reduced by Beilinson–Flach explicit reciprocity and Poitou–Tate to FW's GU(3,1) Theorem 7.32. FW defers the details to Castella–Wan Theorem 3.8, proved there for weight 2, which no stage plans. As written, L1 and AC L1 direct a worker to build SU plus a refinement that does not exist.

In addition, to deduce the following result from [SU], one would need an argument comparing the canonical period and the Gross period, which might not exist in the relevant literature ... indications on how to reprove theorem 1.6 in a way that bypasses this issue are given in section 4.8.' §4.8: 'prove the two-variable Iwasawa-Greenberg Rankin-Selberg Main Conjecture over K ... by reducing it to the Greenberg type main conjecture (theorem 7.32) via explicit reciprocity law for Beilinson-Flach elements and Poitou-Tate exact sequence. findings.claim: L4e's statement omits a hypothesis of Eischen–Wan: the unramified principal series π_p = π(χ_1,…,χ_r) must have pairwise distinct χ_i. The p-stabilised vector, and hence the family, is unique only under this hypothesis. Theorem 1.2 also assumes π tempered. EW remark on p.34 that temperedness is only a convenience in the pullback computation, but the hypothesis should still be carried until that is proved. As written, L4e targets the construction for every unramified-principal-series cusp representation, which EW do not prove.
findings.evidence: APL L4e: 'Construct the genuinely distinct vector-valued Klingen family, Eisenstein measure, pullback identity and local zeta calculations for a cusp representation of definite GU(r,0), unramified principal series at an odd split p over an imaginary quadratic field.' Eischen–Wan arXiv:1404.7153v2 Thm 1.2 (p.4): 'Let π be a tempered irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GU(r,0) of weight k ... such that πp is the unramified principal series representation π(χ1,...,χr) for characters χ1,...,χr such that the χi’s are pairwise distinct.' Prop. 4.8, proof: 'The uniqueness follows from the assumption that the χi’s are pairwise distinct.' p.34: 'in our discussion for Klingen Eisenstein series we assumed the form we start with is tempered. However this is only for convenience of explicit calculation for pullback formula'.
findings.fix: Add to L4e's statement 'with pairwise distinct Satake characters χ_1,…,χ_r of π_p (regular p-stabilisation)' and 'π tempered, as in EW Thm 1.2 (removable only by the separate argument sketched on p.34)'. Propagate both to the consumers AC L2, L2s and BSD.6a wherever they instantiate L4e.

findings.claim: L2 plans to 'establish the order of growth at every q' as part of the BSW construction over an arbitrary number field. The accepted RS-14 narrowing keeps 'per-place growth'. BSW do not prove this. They say admissibility (growth) is available only for totally real or imaginary quadratic F, under tighter slope conditions and with further sources. For general F they call the right growth notion unclear, and they prove only independence of choices.
findings.evidence: APL L2: 'Construct the automorphic cycles and their distribution-valued evaluations, prove distribution relations, independence of representatives and unit descent, and establish the order of growth at every q.' RS-14 (accepted) L2 keeps: 'Prove unit descent, distribution/norm relations, per-place growth and Theorem 11.1'. The APL acceptance line reads 'the BSW construction for all number fields in its actual small-slope range'. Barrera Salazar–Williams arXiv:1602.06244v3, Introduction (p.4): 'In the case that F is totally real or imaginary quadratic, given slightly tighter conditions on the slope one can prove that the distribution we obtain is admissible ... In the general situation, it is rather more difficult to define the correct notion of admissibility ... We instead settle for proving that our construction is independent of choice'. §12 (p.39): 'one might expect the overconvergent cohomology classes we construct to take values in the smaller space of admissible distributions on OF⊗Zp ... Without the theory of admissibility at hand in the latter situation, however, we cannot show that the distribution constructed in this paper is (in general) unique.'
findings.fix: Split the growth target. For F totally real (with the Leopoldt and slope conditions) and F imaginary quadratic, keep growth and uniqueness, sourced to the works BSW cite ([BS13], [Wil17], or Bergdall–Hansen). For general F, state only BSW's independence of choices (Prop. 9.6 and §12), and record per-prime growth as an open statement rather than a BSW target. Also reword L0's uniqueness clause and the APL acceptance line.
